speakers.name: Deanna Kovar
speakers.title: President, Worldwide Agriculture & Turf Division, Production & Precision Ag, Sales and Marketing, Regions of the Americas and Australia

exchanges.analyst: None (management-led prepared segment, no analyst question)
exchanges.question: No analyst question: exchange 1 holds the company's scripted remarks and segment discussion on Q3 results, outlook, tariffs, C&F, Small Ag & Turf, Production & Precision Ag, early order programs, channel inventory and precision technology.
exchanges.answer: Net sales and revenues up 5% to $12.608 billion, equipment operations net sales up 6% to $10.999 billion with 14.4% operating margin, net income $1.379 billion or $5.10 per diluted share. FY2026 net income guide raised to $4.75 billion-$5 billion and equipment operations cash flow to $5 billion-$5.5 billion; tariff refunds of $382 million recognized year to date and direct tariff expense now about $1.1 billion. MY2027 planter and sprayer early orders are up mid-single digits versus last year's completed programs, and management believes 2026 is the bottom of the ag equipment cycle with a measured recovery.

exchanges.question: How should production versus retail by region be viewed for 2027 setup? What are the pricing expectations for 2027 given the early order program is up mid-single digits and inflation concerns on equipment?
exchanges.answer: Seibert: PPA and C&F are both modestly underproducing in 2026, call it a couple of percentage points each; shipping plans are set for the full year, South America drives more caution, and C&F orders are four to five months out. Kovar: EOP pricing was rolled out several months ago and the focus remains on covering inflation across EOP products and the PPA portfolio into 2027. No specific 2027 price percentage given.

exchanges.question: What drove the tariff expectation falling to $1.1 billion, roughly $100 million lower than previously expected: July tariff relief or expected refunds? Also, how is the Deere-designed excavator launch trending and when does broader adoption come?
exchanges.answer: Seibert: the FY2026 annual run rate moves from $1.2 billion to $1.1 billion excluding refunds, mainly from Section 232 changes cutting the rate on imported goods from roughly 25% to 15%, especially for European imports; effective 1st June, so only five of 12 months are in this year, and 2027 gets a further tailwind. Norwood: first Deere-designed excavator models launched earlier this spring, three models in the market, feedback very positive, more models rolling out over the next three to four years, early days.

exchanges.question: Did anything slip or pull forward between 3Q and 4Q, given tractor inventory-to-sales appears to have built in 3Q ahead of the industry? What is the cadence exiting the year?
exchanges.answer: Seibert: do not read too much into Q3; shipment plans were set for the year and some demand was pulled ahead to manage Q4 risk, with nothing to be concerned about on inventory. Kovar: factories are hitting forecasts and sold-ahead positions and retail pace in the Americas are on trend with historical averages. Norwood: Q4 net sales similar to Q3 for PPA and C&F; no refund benefit in Q4; PPA and SAT margins come in a little because of seasonally higher R&D and SA&G in Q4.

exchanges.question: How could mix, including higher technology take rates in C&F and precision ag early orders, affect 2027, compared with the 2- to 3-point mix benefit discussed in prior years?
exchanges.answer: Seibert: the industry environment is still uncertain (input and commodity volatility, Black Sea shipment disruptions, softness in the E.U. and Brazil), and it is too early to tell on mix, especially in South America where things can turn quickly. C&F fundamentals are good, EOP signals including tech adoption will drive mix depending on how they wrap up, and management is encouraged. No mix point figure given.

exchanges.question: What variability by region is behind the early order program, which came in better than expected, and could the mid-single-digit growth wind up in the high single-digit range as the programs close?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Worldwide Ag & Turf, PPA, Sales and Marketing, Americas and Australia
exchanges.answer: Kovar: the programs are still open with a couple of weeks left on sprayers and a little longer on planters; the U.S. is trending slightly better than Canada (a very limited part of planter portfolio); time will tell whether mid-single digits turns more positive. The best signal is technology take rates, with See & Spray factory-installed orders doubling and 40% of planters taking the most advanced technologies.

exchanges.question: What is driving the cadence of early order programs being up mid-single digit: improved grain prices, or technology decisions?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Worldwide Ag & Turf, PPA, Sales and Marketing, Americas and Australia
exchanges.answer: Kovar: would not read much into cadence, which has been as expected; tweaks were made to the early order program this year to give dealers more choice; pleasantly surprised by technology take rates; hopeful the mid-single-digit increase extends well into the year.

exchanges.question: What are 8 Series tractor orders showing in North America? How should Europe be viewed given heat and input cost stress, and would it react like the U.S. to a crop price response?
exchanges.answer: Seibert: 8R orders are as expected, orders run four to five months out and the model year 2026 shipment schedule is basically closed; encouraged by commodity prices, with corn futures about $5.05. In Brazil Deere takes a three-month order book, has Q4 orders on hand and has changed its industry guide; it is too early to tell for 2027, and the financing program at single-digit rates may help. Europe is mixed: arable farmers more challenged, Small Ag & Turf supported by dairy and livestock cash flows; overall order pace as expected with no step-up in the last day or two.

exchanges.question: How are the C&F order programs shaping up, and how much is dealer rental fleet loading?
exchanges.answer: Seibert: C&F order trends are very positive, with about four to five months of orders on hand versus the typical two to three months, which is a little more than wanted. Drivers are large infrastructure projects, data center starts, the independent rental channel and dealer-owned rental fleets; modest underproduction in 2026 sets up an opportunity in 2027. No split of rental fleet loading was quantified.

exchanges.question: Comparing 2026 and 2027, with roughly an $800 million net tariff impact this year, is net tariff impact a headwind, tailwind or neutral for 2027?
exchanges.answer: Norwood: net tariffs will be a headwind next year. About $1.1 billion of direct tariffs this year less $382 million of refunds is approximately $750-ish of net exposure; 2027 run rate is closer to right around $1 billion, so a step up in tariff expense versus this year.

exchanges.question: Why does C&F guidance imply roughly 50 basis points of positive price in Q4 versus +8% in Q3? Does Deere want to grow dealer rental, and how would that change the economics?
exchanges.answer: Seibert: the C&F price guide went 2.5%, 3%, 2.5% and is now back at the full-year guide; Q3 was 8% partly on easy comps, since Q3 2025 had about 5% negative price from incentives; Q4 has nothing outsized and pricing is going well. Norwood: sees opportunity to increase rental exposure; 30%-35% of earthmoving transactions start as a rental; dealer-owned fleets are growing and could help boost inventory fill next year.

exchanges.question: On EOP pricing covering inflation, what about merchandising incentives and the direction of margins into next year? What does the FTC settlement on right to repair mean for the aftermarket and lifecycle solutions business?
exchanges.answer: Seibert: taking measured inflationary price, committed to cover inflation over time, nothing outsized; pricing is set at several points in the year; suppliers pass on tariffs and oil moves. No comment on incentives or directional margin backlog. Norwood: Deere has always supported customers repairing their own equipment, the agreement formalizes tools like Operations Center PRO Service (diagnostics, digital manuals, software updates), and it will support lifecycle solutions long term; no figure given.

exchanges.question: Could the 2028 EU CAP policy change pull demand forward into 2027 or delay European purchases? Any directional forecast for Europe in 2027?
exchanges.answer: Seibert: too early to tell. Order books run four to five months out and Q1 orders are just starting; arable sentiment depends on input costs and commodity prices; dairy and livestock look fairly stable. No pull-forward or delay view and no 2027 forecast.

exchanges.question: How are Brazilian and U.S. farmers positioning on input costs and how will that affect crop and purchase decisions?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Worldwide Ag & Turf, PPA, Sales and Marketing, Americas and Australia
exchanges.answer: Kovar: input uncertainty is global and fertilizer affects Brazilian and U.S. farmers differently; farmers are looking for alternatives in products, amounts and sourcing, remain resilient, and are not cutting intended application much, still focused on yield. Larger farmers have multiple years of inputs contracted and are considering changes.
